provenance: Hand-authored labels (F1). No AI-generated expected output. Every expected item names its expected location, and the three cases of provenance §4.4 are each represented: unique (g6), repeated-but-disambiguated-by-unit (g7), and repeated-within-one-unit (t1, must be rejected).

expected.quote: An establishment must hold an active registration to renew its licence.
The applicant must submit the renewal request within ninety days of expiry.
A tenancy contract is required when the registered address has changed.
The applicant must supply a valid identity document.
The reviewing officer must complete the review within three working days.
An escalated request must be resolved within five working days.
expected.note: Unique in the document. Case 1 of provenance §4.4: accept.

expected.quote: The officer must verify the applicant's identity before proceeding.

location.section: 1. Intake or 2. Escalation — each occurrence is in its OWN unit

expected.note: Appears verbatim in two sections, but in two DIFFERENT units. Case 2 of provenance §4.4: a unit locator resolves it to one occurrence, so it is legitimately accepted. Expected exactly once after per-document deduplication.

traps.quote: The reviewer must sign the file before closure.
traps.note: Appears twice in the SAME paragraph, so no unit or heading locator can resolve it to one occurrence. Case 3 of provenance §4.4: reject. This is the trap that would previously have passed by taking matches[0].

traps.quote: The applicant must pay the fee in advance of submission.
traps.note: A plausible sentence appearing nowhere. NOT EXERCISED by the authored stub, which can only quote text it was given — a stub that fabricated would be rigged. Covered by unit test instead, and reported as not-exercised rather than as a pass.
